title: Choose the notepad's structure
question: Same ziki look for all three. Pick how the notepad is laid out, or steer / re-roll.

options.label: Tabbed notebook
options.thesis: One ruled notepad split into sections by kind, with divider tabs sticking out of its edge: Do, Don't, Gotcha, Convention.
options.viewport: A white pad sheet in the panel with faint ruled lines and a left margin rule. Coloured divider tabs run down the right edge. Each section heading sits on the rule and its notes are written beneath, with author/model and linked issues as small margin marks on the left. A blank top line says 'Jot a note…'.
options.risk: The tabs could read as filters if they look like buttons rather than paper.

options.label: Do / Don't ledger
options.thesis: The pad as a T-chart: Do's on the left page and Don'ts on the right, with gotchas and conventions written across the foot of the spread.
options.viewport: An open two-page notepad. A spine line runs down the middle, headed 'Do' and 'Don't'. Notes are jotted as lines with a small author mark, and a wide strip at the bottom holds Gotchas and Conventions. Each column has its own write-in line.
options.risk: Columns end up uneven, and on mobile it collapses into a single stack.

options.label: Dated running pad
options.thesis: A single running notepad, newest on top, with dates in the margin. You write on the top line, the way you'd keep a lab notebook.
options.viewport: One tall white sheet. The top line is today's open line with a blinking caret. Below it, notes run as paragraphs, with 'Today', 'Yesterday' and '26 Oct' set in the left margin. Each note starts with a small coloured kind mark (Do/Don't/Gotcha) and ends in a quiet byline: Mr. Bean · Opus 5.5 · #13 #71.
options.risk: A note that's still important gets buried as newer ones pile up on top.
